evidence.note: Diagnosed that declaring react/react-dom as vinext dependencies caused a duplicate React copy and invalid hook calls; reworked packaging to peerDependencies and re-ran the full suite — a genuine foundational resolution/packaging pivot with re-verification.
Reworked renderApp to await async server components before renderToString and pass plain params, revisiting a render-pipeline design decision rather than patching individual routes.

On duplicate-runtime/AsyncLocalStorage divergence: tried configFile:false (subsystem rework) but then settled for a globalThis context fallback — a workaround around the underlying multiple-instance resolution flaw rather than fixing resolution.

The custom-server render pipeline never gained real hydration despite being repeatedly identified as the top blocker; the agent piled hacks (event delegation, DOM-text refresh keyed on testids, a global counter fallback script) instead of refactoring the foundation — patching around a flawed core and drifting toward overfit.
Fixed layout-wrapping order and root page->'/' scanner bug as targeted subsystem corrections, showing local design revision but not foundational pivots.

reasoning: The agent demonstrates clear 5-level behavior: it recognized several wrong approaches and reworked those subsystems (React peerDependencies to kill duplicate React, awaiting async components, config-file loading, layout order) rather than only patching symptoms. However it falls short of 8/10 because the single most consequential foundational choice — the SSR render pipeline lacking real client hydration — was repeatedly identified as blocking many subsystems yet never refactored; instead the agent accreted increasingly hacky workarounds (culminating in a hand-written counter fallback script) and a globalThis context shim rather than fixing module resolution. The trajectory is thus a mix of genuine subsystem reworks and a sustained failure to pivot on the core, placing it squarely at 5.
